chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr al-Nahhas, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding the man who copulates,
so his garment falls off from him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.يُجَامِعُ: He copulates / engages in sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man's clothes fall off during sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the loss of clothing during sexual intercourse is deemed inconsequential to ritual purity, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor physical disruptions do not invalidate the core act unless specified. This highlights the practical ease (yusr) in marital relations, distinguishing between essential purity requirements and incidental occurrences. The ruling underscores that the validity of the act relies on the presence of major impurity (janabah) rather than the state of one's garments.
